elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rewritten 14.2.2 reads "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ". The former gates ($60 million of Development Costs funded; before first Regulatory Approval) are deleted, so the election is unconditional. There are no Order Forms in this co-development structure, so the Agreement-level right is sufficient. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a mechanical alias miss (the customer is styled "PB", not a listed alias); on inspection the operative right is expressly present.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ" replaces the redacted [***] notice period; 30 days is within the preferred ceiling and the period is now a defined, exercisable trigger rather than an undisclosed one.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case SFJ will refund to PB, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by PB for the period after the effective date of termination" — the refund is expressly pro rata (not merely a post-termination period refund), runs from Vendor to Customer, and is tied to the convenience termination in the same sentence.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: New clause: "No Termination for Convenience by SFJ. SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term." Term is defined at 14.1, so the temporal anchor is defined. SFJ's retained exits at 14.2.3 (Material Adverse Event), 14.2.6 (Change of Control) and 14.2.10 (JSC disagreement) each depend on a stated event trigger, so they are not convenience rights and do not contradict the new bar.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is thirty (30) days, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band (and better for Customer). Fallback element not satisfied on its literal terms; irrelevant because the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: 14.2.2 retains "an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination", plus continuing Approval Payment exposure. No three-months-of-fees cap exists, so the fallback fee element fails; the drafter offers this cap commercially in the comment only, which does not count as operative language.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Satisfied a fortiori: the inserted clause bars SFJ from any convenience termination during the Term, which is stricter than an end-of-term-only right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: SFJ has no convenience termination right at all under the rendered text, so no notice period is required for one. Explained rather than treated as an omission.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language (unconditional PB convenience right, 30 days' written notice, express pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts, and an express bar on SFJ convenience termination during the Term).

Minimality holds: operation 1 edits only the gating and notice words of 14.2.2's first sentence and adds the refund; operation 2 is a concise insertion needed for the Vendor-side element. No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories, or procedural boilerplate was added, and the retained 300% Development Cost formula, Approval Payment mechanics, Section 11.1.1.4 purchase construct and Sections 14.2.3 / 14.2.6 / 14.2.10 were left untouched rather than trimmed.

Intent preserved: SFJ's event-triggered exits and their payment formulas survive without contradiction with the new no-convenience bar, and cross-references (including Section 5.2.2.2 to 14.2.10, and 6.2 / 6.7 / 11.1.1.4) remain intact with no dangling term. Deleting the pre-first-Regulatory-Approval window does not orphan the retained sentence about continuing development after termination.

Residual commercial point, correctly handled in the comment rather than the redline: the retained 300% of Development Costs exit payment means the convenience right is not penalty-free, but a fee cap is a fallback-level element and is not required for preferred completeness. If negotiation moves to the fallback, the drafter must then insert an operative cap of three months' fees and a 60–90 day notice period — offering them in the margin comment alone would not satisfy that level.

Housekeeping only (not a defect affecting completeness): the inserted Vendor clause renders without its section number; confirm it is numbered (e.g., 14.2.11) in the executed draft so the reference in the comment matches the operative text.
